title: Adding transaction savepoints interpolated the caller-supplied savepoint name into SAVEPOINT/ROLLBACK TO/RELEASE statements with f-strings.

findings.explanation: The savepoint name is interpolated directly into SQL strings using f-strings in multiple places: `SAVEPOINT {name}`, `ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT {self.name}`, and `RELEASE SAVEPOINT {self.name}`. The `name` parameter in `savepoint()` is optional and defaults to an auto-generated safe value, but callers can pass an arbitrary string. If attacker-controlled input reaches `savepoint(name=user_input)` or `rollback_to(savepoint_name=user_input)`, SQL injection is possible. SAVEPOINT names are identifiers, not values, so parameterized queries typically don't apply — the fix would be strict allowlisting/validation of the name (alphanumeric + underscore only).

evidence.content:
async def rollback_to(self):
        await self.transaction.connection.execute(
            f"ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT {self.name}"
        )

    async def release(self):
        await self.transaction.connection.execute(
            f"RELEASE SAVEPOINT {self.name}"
        )

async def savepoint(self, name: t.Optional[str] = None) -> Savepoint:
        name = name or f"savepoint_{self.get_savepoint_id()}"
        await self.connection.execute(f"SAVEPOINT {name}")

async def rollback_to(self):
        await self.transaction.connection.execute(
            f"ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT {self.name}"
        )

    async def release(self):
        await self.transaction.connection.execute(
            f"RELEASE SAVEPOINT {self.name}"
        )

findings.suggested_fix: Validate savepoint names against a strict allowlist pattern (e.g., `re.fullmatch(r'[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*', name)`) before interpolating into SQL, raising a ValueError for invalid names. Alternatively, quote/escape the identifier using the database driver's identifier quoting mechanism.

findings.explanation: This diff introduces transaction savepoint management (internal database engine plumbing). It does not implement any HTTP endpoints, route handlers, or access-control logic. There is no user identity, resource ownership, or authorization decision involved.
